evidence.summary: 为编码 Agent 安装角色与 Skill，并用 SQLite 构建图协调任务依赖、租约、范围验证和 Git 提交。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 README.zh-CN.md、bin/cli.mjs、package.json、src/db/claim.mjs、src/db/commitLock.mjs、src/db/crossBranch.mjs、src/db/gate.mjs、src/db/init.mjs、src/db/plan.mjs、src/db/reconcile.mjs、src/db/verify.mjs、src/hosts/index.mjs、src/registry/cores.json、src/registry/fetch.mjs、src/skills/hedgehog-orchestrating/SKILL.md；CLI复制/生成角色与Skill→core/intents编译SQLite依赖图→lease/冲突claim→宿主Agent按packet执行→scope/真实命令/Git提交→DB完成；非CLI常驻模型loop，见 [Q02](#research-q02)-[Q04](#research-q04)。
limitations: 根package/Host registry/外部DSH core条目、CLI init文件与db/Git写入；core npm pack/tar；plan/claim/snapshot/lease；verify真实exec/scope/noop/Git与DB；commit lock/gate诊断/代表跨branch subject与reconcile。未执行或全258文件、外部core、宿主权限/模型loop、全部计划/override/重建/worktree merge/发行安全。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: 愿意声明intent/scope/verify并审Git的仓库维护者，在可弃置新仓单任务试纪律，见 [Q01](#research-q01)/[Q06](#research-q06)。
CLI复制/生成角色与Skill→core/intents编译SQLite依赖图→lease/冲突claim→宿主Agent按packet执行→scope/真实命令/Git提交→DB完成；非CLI常驻模型loop，见 [Q02](#research-q02)-[Q04](#research-q04)。

根package/Host registry/外部DSH core条目、CLI init文件与db/Git写入；core npm pack/tar；plan/claim/snapshot/lease；verify真实exec/scope/noop/Git与DB；commit lock/gate诊断/代表跨branch subject与reconcile。未执行或全258文件、外部core、宿主权限/模型loop、全部计划/override/重建/worktree merge/发行安全。
CLI开发流程基础设施与宿主角色/Skill资源；有外部DSH开发core registry项，但根无DSH bundle/runtime接线。

#### 依赖

| 条件 | 用途 | 边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node>=22.5/node:sqlite/Git | CLI/图/提交 | 成品兼容未跑 |
| 编码Agent宿主/模型 | 真实执行角色 | CLI无自治模型loop |
| 审过的core/intent/scope/verify | 图编译/命令依据 | shell文本可执行，外部包另审 |
| npm/tar/registry或本地core | 获取模板 | range解析版本非来源安全保证 |
| 可写仓与空index/备份 | 文件/DB/Git | 非跨资源事务 |
| 人工需求/差异/目标验收 | 最后INTENT CHECK | 测试green非任务全成 |

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金/资源 | 人工与未知 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 首次 | 依赖/可选core/模型 | 学习图/声明scope/授权/备份 |
| 持续 | 模型Token/测试/磁盘 | 需求/任务粒度/图和回归 |
| 失败 | 重跑/进程/提交分离 | lease/index/DB恢复，工时未知 |
| 退出 | 记录/模板保留 | 停执行者/逐文件diff恢复 |
可弃置新仓一层任务，审verify命令与自动commit并保空index；不跑并发/外部core/目标worktree，状态或index不明先停执行者退手工清单与测试，见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

#### 效果

| 项目 | 当前支持 | 未验证 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 协调 | 依赖/lease/冲突程序筛选 | 声明真实/多Agent效果 |
| 验证 | scope与真实shell退出码 | 用户目标/命令充分 |
| 完成 | Git/DB/部分noop/reconcile来源 | 所有complete同强度不成立 |
| 持久 | SQLite事务/历史恢复线索 | Git+DB共同原子/掉电 |
| 收益 | 可查小任务交接 | Token/速度/质量净收益 |
SQLite事务/租约与命令/Git链可审，scope指纹和冲突是合作协调；noop/手工完成、跨branch subject与Git/DB分离应保真，见 [Q03](#research-q03)-[Q05](#research-q05)。
把intent/依赖/范围/租约/验证和commit记录接成可查询交接，协调者有真实程序入口而非只信done，见 [Q03](#research-q03)-[Q04](#research-q04)。
verify会执行shell并自动commit，noop可不跑测试、reconcile有人判断路径，Git与DB非共同事务；index/lease/外部writer和业务验收不能靠complete证明，见 [Q04](#research-q04)-[Q05](#research-q05)。
提交前只读核完整index归属，拒绝未许可异task暂存而不自动reset，和现范围门/人工cached diff对照，误归属不降或误拒更重即否定，见 [Q07](#research-q07)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)-[Q03](#research-q03)DAG/lease/模板/TDD成熟，Agent纪律局部组合使novelty25%超0，非新规划/执行范式不达50%。mechanism50%，[Q03](#research-q03)-[Q04](#research-q04)真实claim/范围/命令/提交门超25%纯prompt，旁路/跨资源/效果未验不达75%。transferability50%，角色与图状态/验证分开可迁移超25%某宿主模板，其他core/Host未验不达75%。simplification25%，查询图减少对话记忆超0，维护图/命令/Git/恢复[Q06](#research-q06)仍重不达50%。

business.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)-[Q04](#research-q04)从对话清单改为协调者领带lease packet、宿主worker执行、协调者程序核范围/命令并解锁下游，任务组织/交接职责实际改变，workflow25%超0便利；生产协作/多角色效果未验不达50%。delivery25%，以层任务的验证/commit/artifact和intent最后核对作为交接单元，超0仅聊天答复；[Q04](#research-q04)-[Q05](#research-q05)noop/人工完成和业务验收限制不达50%稳定保障。reach0无此前受限明确人群约束解除，不因多Host达到25%。economics0，[Q06](#research-q06)省Token/更快未测且未改变供给或服务结构，不达25%。

recommendation.reason: 接受显式任务图和 Git 纪律的仓库维护者，可在可弃置小仓用一层可信任务试用。它把委派、范围、验证命令和提交记录接成可查询交接单元。若验证命令、完整 index 或任务与实际代码状态不明，应停新派发并核真实进程和提交，再退回手工清单与测试。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)/[Q06](#research-q06)仓库维护/单层交接与结果明确，50%超25%泛Agent框架；真实项目需求/成效未验不达75%。

advantage.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)-[Q04](#research-q04)真实图/lease/验证提交超25%prompt模板，50%；index/目标验收/恢复限制不达75%。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)-[Q05](#research-q05)实际文件/SQLite/exec/Git/失败链已核，50%超25%声明；未运行Host/core/并发/故障不达75%。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04)-[Q06](#research-q06)shell/自动提交/图与恢复负担重，25%不达50%轻量；可弃置单任务/空index与手工退路超0。

publication.summaries.text: 为编码 Agent 安装角色与 Skill，并用 SQLite 构建图协调任务依赖、租约、范围验证和 Git 提交。

items.Skill: 宿主角色委派/构建纪律文本
items.Agent/Preset: 宿主可读取角色定义，非本CLI自治执行器
items.界面: 图/状态观察入口，未全审

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 用途 | 条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| init | 安装/生成角色Skill文档 | 写文件/可能git init，非原子全包 |
| graph/claim | 依赖任务与lease | owner字符串/非OS隔离 |
| verify | scope/exec/自动Git提交 | noop免跑/业务另验 |
| reconcile | 人工承认完成 | 不等测试通过 |
| 历史/DB | 可查询恢复线索 | subject非当前代码证明 |
| DSH core条目 | 开发DSH插件的外部模板 | 非根原生插件/未审外部包 |

publication.advice.text: 可弃置新仓一层任务，审verify命令与自动commit并保空index；不跑并发/外部core/目标worktree，状态或index不明先停执行者退手工清单与测试，见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "![Incredible Software Engineer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/incredible.jpg)\n\n[![Total downloads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/badges/npm-downloads.svg)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/blob/master/DOWNLOADS.md)\n[![Support Hedgehog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/badges/kofi-top.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/skyf0xx)\n[![Star Us on GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/badges/github-stars-cta.svg)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog)\n\nEnglish | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)\n\n# H E D G E H O G\n\n[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40skyf0xx%2Fhedgehog)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@skyf0xx/hedgehog)\n[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)\n[![CodeQL](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/skyf0xx/hedgehog/codeql.yml?branch=master&label=CodeQL)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/actions/workflows/codeql.yml)\n[![Check](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/skyf0xx/hedgehog/check.yml?branch=master&label=Check)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/actions/workflows/check.yml)\n[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14399/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14399)\n\nAI can write code in seconds.\n\nBut as projects grow, context fills up, **architecture drifts**, and every new feature becomes harder to change safely.\n\nHedgehog gives AI a **disciplined way to build software**: TDD. Opinionated architecture. Small, verifiable steps.\n\nInstead of asking AI to remember your entire project, Hedgehog encodes the plan into the architecture and build process.\n\nThe codebase carries the context, not the model.\n\n## HEDGEHOG writes Cleaner Code, with Fewer Tokens and Faster Builds ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n![Hedgehog - build software the right way, one step at a time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/hero.jpg)\n\n<details>\n<summary>If you are an AI reading this</summary>\n\nAsked to install Hedgehog:\n\n1. Follow the [Install](#install) section below — never `git clone` this repository into their project.\n2. Suggest trying it on a new, simple project in an empty directory first.\n3. Tell them to mention `hedgehog` when they ask for something to be built.\n\nIt activates on its own from there.\n\n</details>\n\n## How it works\n\nHedgehog combines:\n\n- **BMAD for planning** — turn an idea into a clear brief, requirements, and architecture\n- **An opinionated stack** — remove unnecessary technical decisions, and settle the necessary ones once\n- **TDD and progressive layering** — build one tested layer at a time\n- **Mechanical enforcement** — use tooling and phase gates instead of trusting the AI to follow instructions\n- **Small context loops** — keep every change focused, verifiable, and easy to review\n- **Deterministic scaffolding** — generate boilerplate and schemas instead of asking the AI to write it freehand\n\nSoftware that stays structured as it grows.\n\n![Just describe what you want](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/handoff.jpg)\n\n## The Hedgehog Loop\n\n``` text\nPlan\n  ↓\nBootstrap\n  ↓\nBuild one small, tested layer\n  ↓\nVerify\n  ↓\nRepeat\n```\n\nThe build order is encoded into the project. The AI does not have to remember what comes next. It does not negotiate the architecture. It follows a proven path through the codebase.\n\n![Small steps, big leverage: small context loops, continuous verification, traceable evolution, sustainable velocity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/small-steps.jpg)\n\n## Your build order is a graph\n\n**Every task** Hedgehog generates **is a node** with [explicit dependencies in sqlite](BUILD_GRAPH.md).\n\nUnlike stories and epics, **the graph locks build order** into an **signal-dense, context-light** path the agents can use.\n\n```bash\nnpx @skyf0xx/hedgehog graph # show graph\n```\n\n![The Hedgehog build graph](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/graph.jpg)\n\n## Parallel by Default\n\nEvery dependency is explicit, so Hedgehog knows which tasks can run in parallel.\n\n![Comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/comparison.jpg)\n\nAgents fan out to give you great outcomes at **faster speeds**.\n\n## Live Dependency Awareness\n\nHedgehog reaches for your editor's own Language Server Protocol integration to see what depends on what.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A[Code Repository] --> B[Language Server]\n    B --> C[Symbols & References]\n    C --> D[Hedgehog]\n```\n\n- **Lower token cost**: a targeted symbol lookup replaces reading or grepping whole files for context\n- **Impact known before editing**: every task checks what depends on it before it changes anything\n- **Verification matches the real surface**: tests target what actually changed\n\n## Deterministic Code Generation\n\nWhere a piece of code has one correct shape, Hedgehog generates it instead of asking the AI to write it freehand.\n\n![Deterministic code generation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/deterministic.jpg)\n\n- **Generators over freehand**: schemas, boilerplate, and scaffolding come from generators that create the code\n- **Faster**: no reasoning required to produce a known shape\n- **More correct**: the same input always produces the same, tested output\n- **Fewer tokens**: nothing spent generating code that a template already covers\n\nThe AI is reserved for the parts a generator can't cover.\n\n## What Hedgehog builds\n\n### Full-stack applications\n\nA fixed TypeScript stack with a backend-first, test-driven build order:\n\n``` text\nSchema\n  ↓\nContract\n  ↓\nRepository\n  ↓\nService\n  ↓\nController\n  ↓\nUI\n```\n\nEvery layer is verified before the next begins.\n\n### Landing pages\n\nA structured pipeline for producing distinctive, production-quality landing pages:\n\n``` text\nBrief\n  ↓\nFeeling\n  ↓\nDesign tokens\n  ↓\nSequence\n  ↓\nArtifact\n```\n\n### Web Apps/ PWAs\n\nLocal-first simple mobile compatible web  apps: trackers, journals, planners, etc:\n\n``` text\nSchema\n  ↓\nRepository\n  ↓\nHook\n  ↓\nScreen\n```\n\n### DeepSeek Harness       "content": "![Incredible Software Engineer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/incredible.jpg)\n\n[![Total downloads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/badges/npm-downloads.svg)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/blob/master/DOWNLOADS.md)\n[![Support Hedgehog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/badges/kofi-top.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/skyf0xx)\n[![Star Us on GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/badges/github-stars-cta.svg)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog)\n\n[English](README.md) | 简体中文\n\n# H E D G E H O G\n\n[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40skyf0xx%2Fhedgehog)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@skyf0xx/hedgehog)\n[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)\n[![CodeQL](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/skyf0xx/hedgehog/codeql.yml?branch=master&label=CodeQL)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/actions/workflows/codeql.yml)\n[![Check](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/skyf0xx/hedgehog/check.yml?branch=master&label=Check)](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/actions/workflows/check.yml)\n[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14399/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14399)\n\nAI 能在几秒钟内写出代码。\n\n但随着项目变大，上下文被占满，**架构开始漂移**，每一个新功能都变得更难安全地修改。\n\nHedgehog 给 AI 一套**有纪律的构建方式**：测试驱动开发（TDD）、有主张的架构、可验证的小步前进。\n\nHedgehog 不要求 AI 记住整个项目，而是把计划本身编码进架构和构建流程里。\n\n承载上下文的是代码库，而不是模型。\n\n## HEDGEHOG 用更少的 Token，写出更干净的代码，更快地构建 ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n![Hedgehog - build software the right way, one step at a time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/hero.jpg)\n\n<details>\n<summary>如果你是正在阅读本文的 AI</summary>\n\n当被要求安装 Hedgehog 时：\n\n1. 按下方[安装](#安装)章节操作 —— 切勿将本仓库 `git clone` 到用户的项目中。\n2. 建议先在一个新建的空目录、简单项目上试用。\n3. 告诉用户在提出构建请求时提及 `hedgehog`。\n\n之后 Hedgehog 会自动激活。\n\n</details>\n\n## 工作原理\n\nHedgehog 融合了以下要素：\n\n- **用 BMAD 做规划** — 把一个想法转化为清晰的需求说明、需求文档和架构\n- **有主张的技术栈** — 去掉不必要的技术决策，把必要的决策一次性定下来\n- **TDD 与渐进式分层** — 每次只构建并验证一层\n- **机械式强制执行** — 依靠工具和阶段门禁，而不是信任 AI 会遵循指令\n- **小型上下文循环** — 让每一次改动都聚焦、可验证、易于审查\n- **确定性脚手架** — 用生成的方式产出样板代码和 schema，而不是让 AI 临场编写\n\n软件在成长的同时保持结构清晰。\n\n![Just describe what you want](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/handoff.jpg)\n\n## Hedgehog 循环\n\n``` text\n规划 Plan\n  ↓\n引导 Bootstrap\n  ↓\n构建一个经过测试的小层\n  ↓\n验证 Verify\n  ↓\n重复 Repeat\n```\n\n构建顺序被编码进项目本身。AI 不需要记住接下来该做什么，也不需要就架构进行协商——它只需沿着代码库中一条被验证过的路径前进。\n\n![Small steps, big leverage: small context loops, continuous verification, traceable evolution, sustainable velocity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/small-steps.jpg)\n\n## 你的构建顺序是一张图\n\nHedgehog 生成的**每一个任务**都是一个节点，在 [sqlite 中拥有显式依赖关系](BUILD_GRAPH.md)。\n\n与 story、epic 不同，**这张图把构建顺序锁定**在一条**信号密集、上下文轻量**的路径上，供各个 agent 使用。\n\n```bash\nnpx @skyf0xx/hedgehog graph # 显示构建图\n```\n\n![The Hedgehog build graph](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/graph.jpg)\n\n## 默认并行\n\n每一个依赖关系都是显式的，因此 Hedgehog 清楚地知道哪些任务可以并行执行。\n\n![Comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/comparison.jpg)\n\n多个 agent 并行展开工作，以**更快的速度**交付出色的结果。\n\n## 实时感知依赖关系\n\nHedgehog 借助你编辑器自带的 Language Server Protocol 集成来查看代码间的依赖关系。\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A[代码仓库] --> B[Language Server]\n    B --> C[符号与引用]\n    C --> D[Hedgehog]\n```\n\n- **更低的 token 成本**：精准的符号查找取代了为获取上下文而阅读或搜索整个文件\n- **改动前先知影响**：每个任务在动手前都能查清有哪些代码依赖它\n- **验证匹配真实改动范围**：测试针对实际发生变化的部分运行\n\n## 确定性代码生成\n\n当一段代码只有一种正确形态时，Hedgehog 会直接生成它，而不是让 AI 临场编写。\n\n![Deterministic code generation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/deterministic.jpg)\n\n- **生成优先于临场编写**：schema、样板代码和脚手架都来自生成器\n- **更快**：产出已知形态的代码不需要推理\n- **更正确**：相同的输入始终产出相同的、经过测试的输出\n- **更省 Token**：模板已经覆盖的代码，不再消耗 token 去生成\n\nAI 被留给生成器无法覆盖的部分。\n\n## Hedgehog 能构建什么\n\n### 全栈应用\n\n固定的 TypeScript 技术栈，采用后端优先、测试驱动的构建顺序：\n\n``` text\nSchema\n  ↓\nContract\n  ↓\nRepository\n  ↓\nService\n  ↓\nController\n  ↓\nUI\n```\n\n每一层在进入下一层之前都会被验证。\n\n### 落地页 / Landing Pages\n\n用于产出风格独特、生产级质量落地页的结构化流水线：\n\n``` text\nBrief\n  ↓\nFeeling\n  ↓\nDesign tokens\n  ↓\nSequence\n  ↓\nArtifact\n```\n\n### Web 应用 / PWA\n\n本地优先、简单、移动端兼容的 Web 应用：打卡记录、日记、计划工具等：\n\n``` text\nSchema\n  ↓\nRepository\n  ↓\nHook\n  ↓\nScreen\n```\n\n### DeepSeek Harness 插件\n\n面向 DSH 基于 Cordis 的 agent 框架的工具、hook 和扩展：\n\n``` text\nScaffold\n  ↓\nLogic\n  ↓\nWiring\n  ↓\nSmoke\n  ↓\nBundle\n  ↓\nJoin\n```\n\n### 文案写作\n\n文案的撰写与修改会经过一道机械化的关卡，而不是仅靠提示词：\n\n``` text\nBrief\n  ↓\nDraft ⇄ zod validation()\n  ↓ pass\nShip\n```\n\n### 其他任意类型\n\nCLI、库、浏览器扩展、数据管道等，都会拥有各自的构建顺序。\n\n在可能的情况下，Hedgehog 会在 [`hedgehog-core-authored`](https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-authored/tree/main/skills/hedgehog-core-design/blueprints) 中查找该系统形态对应的、经过验证的成熟蓝图。\n\n### 已有代码库\n\nHedgehog 也可以接入已有仓库。\n\nHedgehog 也可以接入它并未参与构建的仓库。它会读取该仓库，并提出一条构建层次链，用仓库自身的 test/lint/build 命令来验证。\n\n## Hedgehog 为什么有效\n\n![Why Hedgehog works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog/master/docs/images/why.jpg)\n\n## 安装\n\n请你的 agent 安装它，或运行以下命令：\n\n想用 Hedgehog 构建任何东西时，请在请求中提及 `Hedgehog`。\n\n<details>\n<summary>给 AI Agent 的操作说明</summary>\n\n1. 检查已安装 Node >=22.5.0。\n2. 运行上方的安装命令。\n\n</details>\n\n### Claude Code\n\n``` bash\nclaude plugin marketplace add skyf0xx/hedgehog\nclaude plugin install hedgehog\n```\n\n### Gemini CLI\n\n``` bash\ngemini extensions install https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog\n```\n\n### Cursor\n\n``` bash\ngit clone https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog ~/.cursor/plugins/local/hedgehog\n```\n\n然后打开一个项目，描述你想构建的内容，并提及 `hedgehog`。\n\n在没有预热过 pnpm 缓存的新项目上，首次安装可能需要几分钟。\n\n更新方式：\n\n``` bash\nnpx @skyf0xx/hedgehog update\n```\n\n这会刷新指定仓库中已安装的 agent 和 skill（注意：不包含 vendor skills）。\n\n## 为什么选择 Hedgehog\n\n大多数 AI 编程工具优化的是提示词（prompting）。\n\nHedgehog 优化的是 **AI 在其中构建的整个系统**。\n\n| | 原生 AI | BMAD | Hedgehog |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| **规划** | 对话式 | 多 agent 工作流 | BMAD |\n| **架构** | AI 自行决定，容易漂移 | 有文档记录 | 一次决定，之后强制执行 |\n| **构建顺序** | 临场发挥 | 依据文档指引 | 机械式强制执行 |\n| **上下文** | 保存在提示词中 | 庞大的规划文档 | 编码进代码库本身 |\n| **验证** | 可选 | 依赖流程 | 测试与阶段门禁 |\n| **结果** | 代码写得快 | 计划写得好 | 软件足够可靠 |\n\n## 架构\n\nHedgehog 为每个 core 使用固定的技术栈和构建顺序。工具链强制执行架构边界，因此正确性不依赖于 AI 是否记得住指令。\n\n完整设计请参见 [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)，如何构建并注册新的\ncore 请参见 [AUTHORING-CORES.md](AUTHORING-CORES.md)（英文文档）。\n\n## 致谢\n\n- 规划流程运行在 [BMAD-METHOD](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD) 之上。\n\n- Nx skills 改编自 [nx-ai-agents-config](https://github.com/nrwl/nx-ai-agents-config)。\n\n- 动画 skills vendored 自 [gsap-skills](https://github.com/greensock/gsap-skills)。\n\n## 支持 Hedgehog\n\n如果 Hedgehog 帮助你用 AI 构建出更好的软件，**请在 GitHub 上给它一个 ⭐**。\n"

findClaimableTasks builds the index before ever\n// entering one).\nfunction crossBranchClaimableCandidates(db, index) {\n  const candidates = db\n    .prepare(\n      `SELECT t.* FROM tasks t\n       WHERE t.status IN ('planned', 'ready')\n         AND t.lease_owner IS NULL\n         AND EXISTS (\n           SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n           JOIN tasks dep ON dep.id = d.depends_on_task_id\n           WHERE d.task_id = t.id AND dep.status <> 'complete'\n         )\n       ORDER BY t.priority, t.exclusive DESC, t.id`,\n    )\n    .all();\n  if (candidates.length === 0) return [];\n\n  const unsatisfied = db.prepare(UNSATISFIED_DEPENDENCIES_SQL).all();\n  const unsatisfiedByTask = new Map();\n  for (const row of unsatisfied) {\n    if (!unsatisfiedByTask.has(row.taskId)) unsatisfiedByTask.set(row.taskId, []);\n    unsatisfiedByTask.get(row.taskId).push(row);\n  }\n\n  return candidates.filter((candidate) =>\n    unsatisfiedByTask\n      .get(candidate.id)\n      .every((dep) => commitMessageExistsAnywhere({ commit_message: dep.commitMessage }, index)),\n  );\n}\n\n// Exported for ready.mjs, which walks the identical candidate set to\n// simulate this same fan-out without claiming anything.\n//\n// Merges CLAIMABLE_TASKS_SQL's own current-DB-only candidates with the\n// cross-branch set above, then re-sorts to the same `priority, exclusive\n// DESC, id` order the fan-out and every caller depend on — the two source\n// queries are individually ordered but interleaving them requires a single\n// re-sort over the union.\n//\n// `index` is optional: a caller outside any sqlite transaction (ready.mjs,\n// status.mjs) can omit it and this builds one itself. Exported for\n// ready.mjs, which needs the same seed to simulate the fan-out accurately.\nexport function findInFlightTasks(db) {\n  return db.prepare(`SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('building', 'verifying')`).all();\n}\n\nfunction loadTask(db, taskId) {\n  return db.prepare('SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id = ?').get(taskId);\n}\n\n// Expired leases go to `blocked`/`lease_expired`, never back to `ready` —\n// a dead agent may have left half-written files, and silently re-handing\n// that task to a fresh agent starts it from a mess it can't see. Exported\n// for verify.mjs's claimForVerify, which reaps its own task's lease\n// before checking ownership — reaping is otherwise lazy (only run here,\n// from claimTasks), so a build that outlives its lease with no\n// concurrent `claim` call in the interim would otherwise reach `verify`\n// with a technically-expired lease that still matches status/lease_owner\n// and sail through unreaped.\n//\n// Returns the ids it just flipped, as a Set — claimTasks's stop-the-line\n// check uses this to tell a block this very call produced from one that\n// was already sitting there, so a dead agent's lease lapsing doesn't\n// itself become the reason every other module's fan-out refuses.\nexport function reapExpiredLeases(db) {\n  const rows = db\n    .prepare(\n      `\n    UPDATE tasks\n    SET status = 'blocked', blocked_reason = 'lease_expired',\n        lease_owner = NULL, lease_expires_at = NULL, leased_at = NULL,\n        claim_snapshot = NULL\n    WHERE status IN ('building', 'verifying') AND lease_expires_at < datetime('now')\n    RETURNING id\n  `,\n    )\n    .all();\n  return new Set(rows.map((r) => r.id));\n}\n\n// The atomic claim primitive: the WHERE clause re-checks status and\n// lease_owner at UPDATE time, so RETURNING a row (rather than undefined)\n// is the only proof this call won the race against a concurrent claim.\nconst claimOne = (db) =>\n  db.prepare(`\n    UPDATE tasks SET status = 'building', lease_owner = ?, leased_at = datetime('now'),\n      lease_expires_at = datetime('now', '+' || ? || ' minutes'),\n      claim_snapshot = ?\n    WHERE id = ? AND status IN ('planned','ready') AND lease_owner IS NULL\n    RETURNING id\n  `);\n\n// Every `blocked` task in the graph, regardless of module or reason —\n// the fan-out claim's stop-the-line check. Ordered the same as the\n// NEEDS ATTENTION list in status.mjs, so the two never disagree about\n// which tasks are outstanding.\nfunction findBlockedTasks(db) {\n  return db.prepare(`SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE status = 'blocked' ORDER BY priority, id`).all();\n}\n\n// Claims up to `count` ready tasks for `owner`, returning\n// `{ claimed, blocked }`. `count` is a maximum, not a promise — `claimed`\n// may hold fewer tasks than `count`, or none. `blocked` is non-empty only\n// on the stop-the-line refusal below, in which case `claimed` is always\n// empty.\n//\n// Stop-the-line: if any task anywhere in the graph was already `blocked`\n// before this call, the fan-out refuses to claim anything at all, in any\n// module — a blocked task needs a human/agent decision (retry after a\n// fix, or leave it), and handing out fresh work around it makes that easy\n// to ignore indefinitely. Deliberately stricter than dependency-based\n// blocking: an unrelated module isn't literally stuck on the blocked\n// task, but the fan-out stops anyway until it's retried. A targeted\n// `hedgehog claim <task-id>` (claimTask, below) is exempt — that's how\n// the blocked task itself gets reclaimed after `hedgehog retry`.\n//\n// \"Already blocked\" excludes a lease this same call's reapExpiredLeases\n// just flipped: a dead agent's lease can lapse on an unrelated module,\n// and the first `claim` call after that lapse is whichever one happens to\n// discover it. That call still claims normally; the reaped task still\n// lands in `blocked`/`lease_expired` and still needs `hedgehog retry`\n// before it's claimable — only this one call's refusal is skipped. Every\n// `claim` call after it sees the same task still blocked and stops as\n// usual.\n//\n// Fan-out keeps the batch mutually non-conflicting, and non-conflicting\n// with every task already in flight, per conflict.mjs's\n// exclusive/scope/verify predicate (item 11): a candidate that conflicts\n// with anything already accepted into this batch *or* already\n// building/verifying is left ready for a future call rather than claimed\n// alongside it. CLAIMABLE_TASKS_SQL's `lease_owner IS NULL` only keeps an\n// in-flight task out of the candidate pool itself — it does not compare a\n// candidate against that task's scope or verify radius, so in-flight\n// tasks must be seeded into the conflict check explicitly. A race lost to\n// a concurrent claimer (the atomic UPDATE returns undefined) is skipped\n// and doesn't count against `count` — it neither joins the batch nor\n// short-circuits the loop.\nexport function claimTasks(db, { owner, count = 1, leaseMinutes = 45 }) {\n  ensureTaskColumns(db);\n  // Read the working tree *before* BEGIN — this file keeps verify.mjs's\n  // rule that no subprocess runs with a sqlite transaction open. One\n  // snapshot serves the whole batch: they all start from the same tree.\n  // Taking it a moment early can only miss a path dirtied in between,\n  // which leaves that path attributed — the strict direction.\n  const claimSnapshot = snapshotWorkingTree();\n  // Same rule, same reason, for the cross-branch index: buildCrossBranchIndex\n  // shells out to `git log --all` (twice — see crossBranch.mjs), so it is\n  // built here, before BEGIN, and threaded into findClaimableTasks rather\n  // than left to build itself once inside the transaction below.\n  const crossBranchIndex = buildCrossBranchIndex(db);\n\n  return inTransaction(db, () => {\n    const justReaped = reapExpiredLeases(db);\n\n    const blocked = findBlockedTasks(db).filter((task) => !justReaped.has(task.id));\n    if (blocked.length > 0) {\n      return { claimed: [], blocked };\n    }\n\n    const candidates = findClaimableTasks(db, crossBranchIndex);\n    const inFlight = findInFlightTasks(db);\n    const runClaim = claimOne(db);\n    const claimed = [];\n\n    for (const candidate of candidates) {\n      if (claimed.length >= count) break;\n      const against = [...inFlight, ...claimed];\n      if (against.some((accepted) => conflicts(candidate, accepted) !== null)) continue;\n      const result = runClaim.get(owner, leaseMinutes, claimSnapshot, candidate.id);\n      if (result === undefined) continue; // lost the race, skip\n      claimed.push(loadTask(db, candidate.id));\n    }\n\n    return { claimed, blocked: [] };\n  });\n}\n\n// Claims one named task for `owner`, bypassing the fan-out's ordering\n// without bypassing any of its safety rules. The batch claim above walks\n// candidates in `priority, id` order and takes the first non-conflicting\n// set, which means a task that conflicts with everything — an\n// `exclusive: true` layer — is only ever handed out when it happens to\n// sort ahead of every other candidate. Any non-exclusive candidate\n// sorting before it takes the slot instead, on every call, however many\n// times the loop runs: the exclusive task starves. This is the operator's\n// way to say which task to hand out, rather than editing the lease into\n// the database by hand.\n//\n// The four refusals below are exactly the fan-out's own preconditions,\n// checked against one named task instead of a candidate list, and each\n// one returns a reason rather than a bare false — a caller that can't say\n// *why* nothing was claimed is the silent-failure this command exists to\n// replace:\n//   no_such_task            — the id doesn't name a row\n//   not_claimable           — wrong status, or already leased\n//   incomplete_dependencies — a dependency isn't `complete` yet\n//   conflict                — conflicts with a task already in flight\n//   race_lost               — a concurrent claim won the atomic UPDATE\nexport function claimTask(db, taskId, { owner, leaseMinutes = 45 }) {\n  ensureTaskColumns(db);\n  // Same rule as claimTasks: read before BEGIN, no subprocess inside a\n  // transaction. buildCrossBranchIndex shells out to `git log --all`, so\n  // it is built here unconditionally (cheap relative to a `git` process\n  // spawn either way) rather than only on the branch that turns out to\n  // need it, which would otherwise tempt building it lazily from inside\n  // the transaction below.\n  const claimSnapshot = snapshotWorkingTree();\n  const crossBranchIndex = buildCrossBranchIndex(db);\n\n  return inTransaction(db, () => {\n    reapExpiredLeases(db);\n\n    const task = loadTask(db, taskId);\n    if (task === undefined) return { claimed: false, reason: 'no_such_task' };\n\n    if (!['planned', 'ready'].includes(task.status) || task.lease_owner !== null) {\n      return { claimed: false, reason: 'not_claimable', task };\n    }\n\n    // Same cross-branch widening findClaimableTasks's fan-out applies: a\n    // dependency this DB still shows incomplete may already be complete on\n    // trunk or a sibling worktree's branch. Checked here too so a targeted\n    // `hedgehog claim <task-id>` doesn't refuse a task the fan-out would\n    // have happily claimed.\n    const stillIncomplete = incompleteDependencies(db, taskId);\n    const incomplete = stillIncomplete.filter(\n      (dep) => !commitMessageExistsAnywhere(dep, crossBranchIndex),\n    );\n    if (incomplete.length > 0) {\n      return { claimed: false, reason: 'incomplete_dependencies', task, incomplete };\n    }\n\n    // Conflicting with something already building/verifying is the one\n    // refusal a targeted claim must keep: the whole point of the\n    // conflict predicate is that two overlapping tasks in one working\n    // tree corrupt each other's scope check and commit. Waiting for the\n    // neighbor to finish (or releasing it) is the fix, not overriding\n    // this.\n    const conflicting = [];\n    for (const other of findInFlightTasks(db)) {\n      if (other.id === task.id) continue;\n      const kind = conflicts(task, other);\n      if (kind !== null) conflicting.push({ task: other, kind });\n    }\n    if (conflicting.length > 0) {\n      return { claimed: false, reason: 'conflict', task, conflicting };\n    }\n\n    const result = claimOne(db).get(owner, leaseMinutes, claimSnapshot, task.id);\n    if (result === undefined) return { claimed: false, reason: 'race_lost', task };\n\n    return { claimed: true, task: loadTask(db, task.id) };\n  });\n}\n\n// Returns a `blocked` task to `planned`, so it can be claimed and built\n// again. Every blocked_reason is eligible: a failed verification and a\n// scope violation are the loop's expected failure cases (build, gate\n// rejects, fix, retry), and a reaped lease is a dead agent's task that a\n// live one has to be able to pick back up. Without this there is no\n// transition out of `blocked` at all — `releaseTask` only accepts\n// `building`, and `verifyTask` refuses anything that isn't `building`\n// and leased, so a blocked task is unreachable by every other command.\n//\n// `planned` rather than `ready`: it's the status `plan.mjs` writes for a\n// task that hasn't been built yet, and the readiness SELECT accepts both,\n// so the task re-enters the queue exactly where a freshly compiled one\n// would — still subject to its dependencies being complete.\nexport function retryTask(db, taskId) {\n  return inTransaction(db, () => {\n    // Same reason verifyTask reaps before its own status check: a task\n    // whose lease expired with no intervening `claim` call is still\n    // sitting in `building`/`verifying` here, not yet swept to `blocked`\n    // — without this, retry on that task reads \"not blocked\" and refuses,\n    // even though the lease is in fact dead and this is exactly the\n    // situation retry exists to recover from.\n    reapExpiredLeases(db);\n    const task = loadTask(db, taskId);\n    if (task === undefined) return { retried: false, reason: 'no_such_task' };\n    if (task.status !== 'blocked') return { retried: false, reason: 'not_blocked', task };\n\n    const result = db\n      .prepare(\n        `\n        UPDATE tasks SET status = 'planned', blocked_reason = NULL,\n          lease_owner = NULL, lease_expires_at = NULL, leased_at = NULL\n        WHERE id = ? AND status = 'blocked'\n        RETURNING id\n      `,\n      )\n      .get(taskId);\n\n    if (result === undefined) return { retried: false, reason: 'not_blocked', task };\n\n    return { retried: true, from: task.blocked_reason, task: loadTask(db, taskId) };\n  });\n}\n\n// The full transitive closure of tasks that depend on `taskId`, directly\n// or through another dependent — the same walk verify.mjs's\n// loadDirectDependents feeds one layer at a time, extended to every\n// layer downstream. A Correction Protocol reopen has to see this whole\n// chain: an upstream task built on wrong output can have several\n// already-complete layers stacked on it, and every one of them was\n// built against the thing that's about to change.\nfunction loadTransitiveDependents(db, taskId) {\n  const directDependents = db.prepare(\n    'SELECT task_id AS id FROM dependencies WHERE depends_on_task_id = ?',\n  );\n  const seen = new Set([taskId]);\n  const downstream = [];\n  let frontier = [taskId];\n  while (frontier.length > 0) {\n    const next = [];\n    for (const id of frontier) {\n      for (const row of directDependents.all(id)) {\n        if (seen.has(row.id)) continue;\n        seen.add(row.id);\n        downstream.push(row.id);\n        next.push(row.id);\n      }\n    }\n    frontier = next;\n  }\n  return downstream;\n}\n\n// Reopens `taskId` for a Correction Protocol fix: moves a `complete` task\n// (and every `complete` task downstream of it, transitively) back to\n// `planned`, so the fix and every layer built on top of it are rebuilt\n// and re-verified in dependency order, the same as any other `planned`\n// task.\n//\n// This is deliberately not folded into `retryTask` as an automatic extra\n// case: `retry` returns a task the loop itself put into `blocked` —\n// expected, low-stakes, no confirmation needed. Reopening a `complete`\n// task undoes a task the loop already verified and committed, and can\n// invalidate everything built against it since, which is why the CLI\n// requires an explicit `--confirm` before calling this — see\n// `reopenCommand`.\n//\n// A downstream task not yet `complete` (still `planned`, `ready`,\n// `building`, `blocked`) is left exactly where it is: it hasn't shipped\n// anything for the fix to invalidate, and its own lease (if any) is not\n// this command's to touch. Only `complete` tasks — upstream's own status\n// plus every `complete` descendant — move; anything else downstream is\n// reported back so the caller can decide what to do about in-flight\n// work sitting on top of a reopened dependency.\nexport function reopenTask(db, taskId) {\n  return inTransaction(db, () => {\n    reapExpiredLeases(db);\n    const task = loadTask(db, taskId);\n    if (task === undefined) return { reopened: false, reason: 'no_such_task' };\n    if (task.status !== 'complete') {\n      return { reopened: false, reason: 'not_complete', task };\n    }\n\n    const downstreamIds = loadTransitiveDependents(db, taskId);\n    const downstreamTasks = downstreamIds.map((id) => loadTask(db, id));\n    const toReopen = [task, ...downstreamTasks.filter((t) => t.status === 'complete')];\n    const stillInFlight = downstreamTasks.filter((t) => t.status !== 'complete');\n\n    const reopenOne = db.prepare(\n      `\n      UPDATE tasks SET status = 'planned', blocked_reason = NULL,\n        lease_owner = NULL, lease_expires_at = NULL, leased_at = NULL,\n        claim_snapshot = NULL\n      WHERE id = ? AND status = 'complete'\n      RETURNING id\n    `,\n    );\n    const reopenedIds = [];\n    for (const t of toReopen) {\n      const result = reopenOne.get(t.id);\n      if (result !== undefined) reopenedIds.push(result.id);\n    }\n\n    return {\n      reopened: true,\n      reopenedIds,\n      stillInFlight,\n      task: loadTask(db, taskId),\n    };\n  });\n}\n\n// Releases `taskId` back to `ready` if `owner` currently holds its lease.\n// Scoped to `status = 'building'` — `verifying` is the engine's own\n// transient lease during verifyTask, not something an external release\n// call should touch. Unlike lease expiry (a dead-agent scenario that goes\n// to `blocked`), an explicit release is a live agent saying \"I'm done\n// with this, not because it's broken\" — so the task is immediately\n// re-claimable.\nexport function releaseTask(db, taskId, owner) {\n  return inTransaction(db, () => {\n    const result = db\n      .prepare(\n        `\n        UPDATE tasks SET status = 'ready', lease_owner = NULL,\n          lease_expires_at = NULL, leased_at = NULL, claim_snapshot = NULL\n        WHERE id = ? AND lease_owner = ? AND status = 'building'\n        RETURNING id\n      `,\n      )\n      .get(taskId, owner);\n\n    if (result !== undefined) return { released: true };\n    // Which of the two failures this was, so the CLI can say \"no such\n    // task\" instead of implying the id exists but is held by someone\n    // else — a mistyped id and a genuinely un-held task are different\n    // problems with different fixes.\n    const task = loadTask(db, taskId);\n    return { released: false, reason: task === undefined ? 'no_such_task' : 'not_held', task };\n  });\n}\n\n// Extends `taskId`'s lease by `minutes` if `owner` currently holds it,\n// during either `building` or `verifying`.\nexport function renewLease(db, taskId, owner, minutes) {\n  return inTransaction(db, () => {\n    const result = db\n      .prepare(\n        `\n        UPDATE tasks SET lease_expires_at = datetime('now', '+' || ? || ' minutes')\n        WHERE id = ? AND lease_owner = ? AND status IN ('building', 'verifying')\n        RETURNING id\n      `,\n      )\n      .get(minutes, taskId, owner);\n\n    if (result !== undefined) return { renewed: true };\n    const task = loadTask(db, taskId);\n    return { renewed: false, reason: task === undefined ? 'no_such_task' : 'not_held', task };\n  });\n}\n"

      "path": "src/db/commitLock.mjs",
      "content": "// The global commit lock — serializes the git-mutating section of\n// `verifyTask` (scope diff, staging, commit) across concurrent processes.\n// See hedgehog-persistent-build-graph.md, \"Claims\" / concurrent\n// execution: two tasks may build concurrently, but git has one working\n// tree and one index, so the commit phase itself cannot. `.hedgehog/\n// commit.lock` is gitignored in every core's template — it's a runtime\n// mutex, not project state.\n\nimport { openSync, closeSync, unlinkSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { DB_PATH } from './init.mjs';\n\n// Exported so verify.mjs's isEngineStatePath can exclude it from every\n// task's scope check — same reasoning as the DB path itself: this file\n// is engine-internal, and gate 1's diff would otherwise catch its own\n// lock file as an \"offending\" path the instant it's created.\nexport const LOCK_PATH = `${DB_PATH.slice(0, DB_PATH.lastIndexOf('/'))}/commit.lock`;\n\n// A lock file older than this is assumed to belong to a process that\n// crashed before releasing it (no host-level lock survives a kill -9) —\n// stealing it is safer than a build that hangs forever on a dead holder.\nconst STALE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;\nconst POLL_MS = 100;\n\nfunction tryAcquire() {\n  try {\n    // 'wx' is an atomic exclusive create — the one primitive this needs.\n    // Two processes racing this call: exactly one gets the fd, the other\n    // throws EEXIST. That's the whole mutex; no separate locking library\n    // is warranted for one gitignored marker file.\n    const fd = openSync(LOCK_PATH, 'wx');\n    closeSync(fd);\n    return true;\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err.code !== 'EEXIST') throw err;\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction stealIfStale() {\n  try {\n    const { mtimeMs } = statSync(LOCK_PATH);\n    if (Date.now() - mtimeMs > STALE_MS) unlinkSync(LOCK_PATH);\n  } catch {\n    // Gone already (released between the stat and here) — nothing to do.\n  }\n}\n\n// Blocks (synchronously spinning the event loop via a busy wait — this\n// file has no async caller; verifyTask and everything in it is sync by\n// design, see verify.mjs) until the lock is held, then runs `fn` and\n// always releases. A crashed holder's lock is stolen after STALE_MS\n// rather than wedging every future verify permanently.\nexport function withCommitLock(fn) {\n  const deadline = Date.now() + STALE_MS * 2;\n  while (!tryAcquire()) {\n    stealIfStale();\n    if (Date.now() > deadline) {\n      throw new Error(\n        `commit lock (${LOCK_PATH}) held past ${STALE_MS * 2}ms — a stuck verify or a bug in lock release`,\n      );\n    }\n    // Synchronous sleep: Atomics.wait blocks the thread without a promise,\n    // matching this module's fully-synchronous call chain.\n    Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, POLL_MS);\n  }\n  try {\n    return fn();\n  } finally {\n    try {\n      unlinkSync(LOCK_PATH);\n    } catch {\n      // Already gone (stolen as stale while we held it past STALE_MS,\n      // which the deadline check above should prevent, but releasing a\n      // lock that's already gone must not throw over the real result).\n    }\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "src/db/crossBranch.mjs",
      "content": "// Cross-branch commit-history visibility for `hedgehog ready`/`claim`/\n// `status`/`reconcile`, run live inside a `git worktree` checkout — where\n// `hedgehog db rebuild` (rebuild.mjs#loadCommitSubjects) intentionally\n// only ever reads the CURRENT branch's own `git log`.\n//\n// The gap this closes: each worktree carries its own `.hedgehog/hedgehog.db`\n// (worktree.mjs's file header), and no DB row is ever copied between them\n// or from a worktree to trunk — that invariant is the reason the build\n// graph is a pure function of committed files plus git history in the\n// first place. But \"current git history\" was, until now, silently read as\n// \"the current branch's history\" everywhere a live command checked whether\n// a dependency was done: claim.mjs's CLAIMABLE_TASKS_SQL joins only the\n// current DB's own `tasks.status`, and reconcile.mjs's `commitsSince`\n// ranges over `HEAD` alone. A task completed and committed on trunk (or on\n// a sibling worktree's branch) is therefore invisible to a different\n// worktree's own DB even though the *commit* — the actual source of truth\n// — is sitting right there in the same repository's object store, reachable\n// from a local ref this checkout can already see.\n//\n// This module answers the same question rebuild.mjs#loadCommitSubjects\n// answers for the current branch (did a commit with this exact subject\n// ever happen), widened to `git log --all` — every local branch's\n// reachable history, which covers trunk and every open worktree's branch,\n// since a worktree's branch is still a local ref of the same checkout.\n// `--all` is exactly the right and only widening: it costs nothing beyond\n// one extra `git log` flag, needs no new git remotes or fetches, and a\n// project that has never used worktrees has exactly one branch with any\n// commits — `git log --all` degenerates to `git log` for it, so this\n// function is a strict no-op there (acceptance criterion: zero behavior\n// change for a project that never opened a worktree).\n//\n// ── the ambiguous-commit-message case: a documented, deliberate gap ────\n//\n// rebuild.mjs#markCompletedTasks resolves a commit_message shared by more\n// than one task (the linear-chain core case — authored/adopted, no\n// `{module}` axis) via an ordering+consumption fixpoint walk over\n// `dependencies` rows, mutating `tasks.status` directly as it goes. That\n// walk is inseparable from the DB write path it drives (UPDATE statements\n// interleaved with the fixpoint, `reconciledTaskIds` seeded in up front,\n// re-open-on-failed-claim at the end) and rebuild.mjs is explicitly out of\n// scope for this change — re-deriving its `positionOf`/`available`/\n// `ranAfterPrerequisites` machinery here as a read-only, no-mutation\n// sibling would either (a) silently drift from the real algorithm the\n// first time either copy changes, which is exactly the \"three divergent\n// implementations\" this file exists to avoid, or (b) require touching\n// rebuild.mjs to extract a shared core, which the task constraints forbid.\n//\n// So: a task whose `commit_message` is NOT unique across the whole graph\n// (the ambiguous / linear-chain case) is left OUT of `subjectsAllBranches`\n// entirely by this module — see `buildCrossBranchIndex`'s filtering below.\n// Every caller (claim.mjs, ready.mjs indirectly, status.mjs, reconcile.mjs)\n// then treats \"not present in the index\" as \"can't determine — leave\n// blocked\", the safe direction: a cross-worktree dependency this module\n// can't resolve stays exactly as blocked as it already was, never\n// incorrectly unblocked. The module-axis case — the overwhelmingly common\n// one, since it's what `full-stack-app`/`pwa-app`/`landing-page` compile —\n// has a `commit_message` unique to each task by construction (the layer's\n// `commit` template interpolates `{module}`) and is fully solved.\nimport { execSync } from 'node:child_process';\n\n// Memoized per `git log --all` call: a Map from commit subject to the\n// number of times it occurs, newest-history-order irrelevant here (unlike\n// rebuild.mjs's positional Map, this module never needs to order two\n// candidate commits against each other, since it only ever answers for the\n// unambiguous case where any one occurrence is as good as any other).\n// Re-running `git log --all` per call rather than caching across calls:\n// every entry point here (claim, ready, status, reconcile) is invoked at\n// most once per CLI process, so there is no repeated-call cost to amortize\n// within a run, and caching across separate `hedgehog` invocations would\n// risk serving a stale answer to a long-lived process (the graph server)\n// after a sibling worktree commits.\nfunction subjectCountsFrom(gitArgs) {\n  let output;\n  try {\n    output = execSync(`git log ${gitArgs} --topo-order --format=%H%x00%s`, { encoding: 'utf8' });\n  } catch {\n    // No commits reachable from the requested ref set yet (a brand-new\n    // repo, or — for the current-branch-only call — a worktree whose\n    // branch predates its very first commit). Every subject is absent,\n    // which is the correct, honest answer.\n    return new Map();\n  }\n  const counts = new Map();\n  for (const line of output.split('\\n')) {\n    if (!line) continue;\n    const [, subject] = line.split('\\0');\n    if (subject === undefined) continue;\n    counts.set(subject, (counts.get(subject) ?? 0) + 1);\n  }\n  return counts;\n}\n\nfunction loadAllBranchesSubjectCounts() {\n  return subjectCountsFrom('--all');\n}\n\n// The current branch's own subject counts — i.e. exactly what\n// rebuild.mjs#loadCommitSubjects would see (membership only; this module\n// never needs commit position, only \"did this subject occur here at\n// all\"). Used by buildCrossBranchIndex below to detect the one case\n// cross-branch crediting must refuse: a task reopened via the Correction\n// Protocol (claim.mjs#reopenTask) after an EARLIER commit with the same\n// subject already landed on this very branch. That earlier commit is\n// exactly as visible via `--all` as any genuine cross-branch completion —\n// nothing about the subject string distinguishes \"this is a fresh\n// completion on another branch\" from \"this is the stale completion this\n// branch itself already reset\". A task whose current DB status is not\n// `complete` but whose commit_message already appears on THIS branch is\n// therefore excluded from resolvableMessages entirely: crediting it would\n// resurrect a completion this worktree's own history has already\n// superseded, which is worse than the safe \"leave it blocked, the\n// dependency isn't obviously satisfied\" default this whole module commits\n// to elsewhere.\nfunction loadCurrentBranchSubjectCounts() {\n  return subjectCountsFrom('');\n}\n\n// Builds the set of commit_messages this module can safely credit as\n// \"happened somewhere in this repository's visible history\" — i.e. every\n// subject that occurs in `git log --all` AND belongs, in `db`, to exactly\n// one task. A subject occurring for two distinct reasons (two different\n// tasks in this graph legitimately share a commit_message — the ambiguous\n// linear-chain case) is deliberately excluded even though it does appear\n// in history, per the module-header comment above: this function cannot\n// tell which of the sharing tasks a given commit actually credits, and\n// guessing is worse than leaving both blocked.\n//\n// `db` is read only for `tasks.commit_message` grouping — never written.\nexport function buildCrossBranchIndex(db) {\n  const tasks = db.prepare('SELECT id, commit_message, status FROM tasks').all();\n  const messageCounts = new Map();\n  const statusByMessage = new Map();\n  for (const task of tasks) {\n    messageCounts.set(task.commit_message, (messageCounts.get(task.commit_message) ?? 0) + 1);\n    statusByMessage.set(task.commit_message, task.status);\n  }\n\n  const subjectCounts = loadAllBranchesSubjectCounts();\n  const currentBranchCounts = loadCurrentBranchSubjectCounts();\n  const resolvableMessages = new Set();\n  for (const [message, taskCount] of messageCounts) {\n    if (taskCount !== 1) continue; // ambiguous in THIS graph — see header comment\n    const total = subjectCounts.get(message) ?? 0;\n    if (total === 0) continue; // not seen on any branch\n    const onThisBranch = currentBranchCounts.get(message) ?? 0;\n    // Reopen guard (see loadCurrentBranchSubjectCounts): if every\n    // occurrence of this subject anywhere (`total`) is already accounted\n    // for on THIS branch (`onThisBranch >= total`) and the task is still\n    // not `complete` here, there is no occurrence anywhere else to credit\n    // — the one this branch already has is exactly the completion a\n    // Correction Protocol reopen (claim.mjs#reopenTask) superseded, and\n    // `--all` has nothing further to offer. Strictly fewer occurrences on\n    // this branch than `total` means at least one occurrence exists on\n    // SOME other branch this worktree cannot otherwise see, which is\n    // exactly the genuine cross-branch completion this module exists to\n    // surface — trusted even when this branch also independently carries\n    // its own earlier, now-superseded copy of the same subject.\n    if (onThisBranch >= total && statusByMessage.get(message) !== 'complete') {\n      continue;\n    }\n    resolvableMessages.add(message);\n  }\n\n  return { resolvableMessages };\n}\n\n// Returns true if `task` (a `tasks` row carrying `commit_message`, and\n// unique in `db` for that message) can be credited complete from\n// cross-branch history, per the index built above. Callers pass the same\n// `index` across many tasks in one call rather than rebuilding it per\n// task — one `git log --all` per CLI invocation, mirroring\n// rebuild.mjs#loadCommitSubjects's own one-call-per-run shape.\nexport function commitMessageExistsAnywhere(task, index) {\n  return index.resolvableMessages.has(task.commit_message);\n}\n\n// Convenience for a caller that only has a raw commit_message string (no\n// task row) — reconcile.mjs's evidence path doesn't need the\n// per-task-uniqueness guard, since it isn't resolving a *dependency*'s\n// status, only widening the commit window it reads from. Kept separate\n// from commitMessageExistsAnywhere (which is intentionally conservative\n// about ambiguity) so this narrower use doesn't inherit a guard it has no\n// use for.\nexport function anyCommitAnywhereWithSubject(subject) {\n  return (loadAllBranchesSubjectCounts().get(subject) ?? 0) > 0;\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "src/db/gate.mjs",
      "content": "// Is the commit gate actually enforcing? — the second line of defence\n// behind `lefthook.yml`'s own `assert_lefthook_installed`.\n//\n// The gate's whole promise is that it can't be worked around, and its\n// worst failure mode is not a broken hook but an absent one: `.git/hooks`\n// is present, `lefthook.yml` is committed, and nothing in a commit's\n// output distinguishes \"passed the gate\" from \"there was no gate\". Every\n// signal a person would look at says gated. So the check has to be\n// explicit, and it belongs somewhere read at the start of every session\n// — which is `hedgehog status`.\n//\n// Read-only and never throws: a status command that fails because it\n// couldn't stat a hook would be worse than the thing it reports on.\n\nimport { readFile, access } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { constants } from 'node:fs';\nimport { join, isAbsolute, delimiter } from 'node:path';\nimport { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';\n\nconst exists = (p) =>\n  access(p, constants.F_OK).then(\n    () => true,\n    () => false,\n  );\n\n// The string `lefthook install` writes into the generated hook when\n// `assert_lefthook_installed: true` is set. Its presence is the only\n// way to tell a fail-closed hook from a fail-open one, since both are\n// otherwise the same generated script — and the distinction matters,\n// because the flag is baked in at install time, so a hook generated\n// before the flag was set keeps failing open until it's regenerated.\nconst ASSERT_MARKER = 'Operation is aborted due to lefthook settings';\n\n// Resolves the repo's hooks directory the way git itself does, so a\n// project that has moved it with `core.hooksPath`, or is running from a\n// worktree, isn't reported as ungated on the strength of an empty\n// `.git/hooks`. Falls back to the conventional location if git can't be\n// run at all — guessing the usual path is a better failure than\n// announcing \"no gate installed\" because we couldn't spawn a process.\nfunction hooksDir(projectRoot) {\n  try {\n    const out = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-path', 'hooks'], {\n      cwd: projectRoot,\n      encoding: 'utf8',\n      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],\n    }).trim();\n    if (out) return isAbsolute(out) ? out : join(projectRoot, out);\n  } catch {\n    // fall through\n  }\n  return join(projectRoot, '.git/hooks');\n}\n\n// The subset of the generated hook's own lookup chain that can be\n// checked without running anything: the binary on PATH, and the two\n// node_modules layouts lefthook's npm package produces. Deliberately\n// not exhaustive — the hook also tries bundler/go/mise/etc. paths — so\n// this only ever reports \"missing\" for the JS-toolchain install this\n// core actually uses.\nasync function lefthookBinaryPresent(projectRoot) {\n  const dirs = (process.env.PATH ?? '').split(delimiter).filter(Boolean);\n  for (const dir of dirs) {\n    if (await exists(join(dir, 'lefthook'))) return true;\n  }\n  if (await exists(join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/lefthook/bin/index.js'))) return true;\n\n  const osArch = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'windows' : process.platform;\n  const cpuArch = process.arch === 'x64' ? 'x64' : process.arch === 'arm64' ? 'arm64' : process.arch;\n  if (await exists(join(projectRoot, `node_modules/lefthook-${osArch}-${cpuArch}/bin/lefthook`))) {\n    return true;\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\n// Returns { applicable, state, detail, repair }.\n//\n//   applicable false  this core doesn't gate commits with lefthook —\n//                     nothing to report, and reporting \"no gate\" would\n//                     be wrong rather than merely noisy\n//   active            hooks installed, fail-closed, binary resolvable\n//   not-installed     lefthook.yml is committed but no hook was written\n//   fails-open        hook predates assert_lefthook_installed\n//   binary-missing    hook would refuse, but the tooling is gone\nexport async function commitGateStatus(projectRoot) {\n  if (!(await exists(join(projectRoot, 'lefthook.yml')))) {\n    return { applicable: false };\n  }\n\n  const hook = join(hooksDir(projectRoot), 'pre-commit');\n\n  if (!(await exists(hook))) {\n    return {\n      applicable: true,\n      state: 'not-installed',\n      detail: 'lefthook.yml is committed, but no pre-commit hook is installed.',\n      repair: 'pnpm dlx lefthook install',\n    };\n  }\n\n  let script;\n  try {\n    script = await readFile(hook, 'utf8');\n  } catch {\n    // Unreadable is not the same as absent, and guessing which one it\n    // is would be worse than saying so.\n    return {\n      applicable: true,\n      state: 'unknown',\n      detail: `Could not read ${hook}.`,\n      repair: 'pnpm dlx lefthook install',\n    };\n  }\n\n  if (!script.includes(ASSERT_MARKER)) {\n    return {\n      applicable: true,\n      state: 'fails-open',\n      detail:\n        'The installed hook predates assert_lefthook_installed — it exits 0 ' +\n        'when lefthook is missing, so commits land ungated.',\n      repair: 'pnpm dlx lefthook install   (regenerates the hook fail-closed)',\n    };\n  }\n\n  if (!(await lefthookBinaryPresent(projectRoot))) {\n    return {\n      applicable: true,\n      state: 'binary-missing',\n      detail:\n        'The hook is fail-closed, so it will refuse commits until lefthook ' +\n        'is back — nothing is landing ungated, but nothing can land at all.',\n      repair: 'pnpm install',\n    };\n  }\n\n  return { applicable: true, state: 'active' };\n}\n\n// Plain text, colouring left to the caller — same split as formatStatus.\n// Returns null when there's nothing worth printing.\nexport function formatCommitGate(gate) {\n  if (!gate || !gate.applicable) return null;\n  if (gate.state === 'active') return 'COMMIT GATE  active';\n\n  const lines = ['COMMIT GATE  NOT ENFORCING', '', `  ${gate.detail}`, ''];\n  lines.push(`  Restore it with: ${gate.repair}`);\n  lines.push('  To commit anyway, deliberately: git commit --no-verify');\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "src/db/init.mjs",
      "content": "// `hedgehog db init` — creates .hedgehog/hedgehog.db if absent, no-ops if\n// present. See hedgehog-persistent-build-graph.md, \"The CLI is the only\n// writer\".\n\nimport { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';\nimport { mkdir } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';\nimport { constants } from 'node:fs';\nimport { access } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { applySchema } from './schema.mjs';\n\nexport const DB_PATH = '.hedgehog/hedgehog.db';\n\nconst exists = (p) =>\n  access(p, constants.F_OK).then(\n    () => true,\n    () => false,\n  );\n\nexport const dbAbsPath = (root = process.cwd()) => resolve(root, DB_PATH);\n\n// One place every CLI command opens the build graph from, so the\n// per-connection pragmas below (busy_timeout, WAL) are never skipped at\n// a call site that forgot them. journal_mode is skipped for read-only\n// handles — it requires write access and a readOnly connection has no\n// business changing the file's journal mode anyway.\n//\n// applySchema also runs here, not only from `dbInit`: a graph created by\n// an older CLI version is missing whatever tables/columns shipped since,\n// and every command besides `init`/`update` opens the graph straight\n// from here rather than going through dbInit first. Without this, those\n// commands only see the fix after someone thinks to rerun `init` on an\n// already-initialized project — which nothing prompts them to do — and\n// until then every query naming a newer column fails with \"no such\n// column\". Skipped for read-only handles for the same reason\n// journal_mode is: it requires write access, and a readOnly caller is\n// only ever reached after a writable open earlier in the same command.\nexport function openDb({ readOnly = false } = {}) {\n  const db = new DatabaseSync(dbAbsPath(), { readOnly });\n  db.exec('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON');\n  db.exec('PRAGMA busy_timeout = 10000');\n  if (!readOnly) db.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL');\n  db.exec('PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL');\n  if (!readOnly) applySchema(db);\n  return db;\n}\n\nexport function withDb(fn, opts) {\n  const db = openDb(opts);\n  try {\n    return fn(db);\n  } finally {\n    db.close();\n  }\n}\n\n// openDb's cwd-relative counterpart for the one caller that has to open a\n// build graph that is deliberately not the one `process.cwd()` names:\n// `hedgehog merge` reads a worktree's own `.hedgehog/hedgehog.db` (its\n// completeness check) while running from trunk's checkout. Same pragmas,\n// same schema-apply-on-writable-open contract as openDb — the only\n// difference is the path is given rather than resolved from DB_PATH.\nexport function openDbAt(absPath, { readOnly = false } = {}) {\n  const db = new DatabaseSync(absPath, { readOnly });\n  db.exec('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON');\n  db.exec('PRAGMA busy_timeout = 10000');\n  if (!readOnly) db.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL');\n  db.exec('PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL');\n  if (!readOnly) applySchema(db);\n  return db;\n}\n\n// BEGIN IMMEDIATE rather than a bare BEGIN: acquires the write lock up\n// front instead of on the first write statement, so two concurrent\n// writers fail fast with SQLITE_BUSY (retried via busy_timeout) instead\n// of deadlocking each other mid-transaction.\nexport function inTransaction(db, fn) {\n  db.exec('BEGIN IMMEDIATE');\n  try {\n    const result = fn();\n    db.exec('COMMIT');\n    return result;\n  } catch (err) {\n    try {\n      db.exec('ROLLBACK');\n    } catch {\n      // Rollback failing must not mask the original error.\n    }\n    throw err;\n  }\n}\n\n// Returns { created: boolean, path } — created is false when the DB file\n// already existed (no-op per the spec).\nexport async function dbInit(dbPath = DB_PATH) {\n  const already = await exists(dbPath);\n  await mkdir(dirname(dbPath), { recursive: true });\n\n  const db = new DatabaseSync(dbPath);\n  try {\n    db.exec('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;');\n    // Applied unconditionally, not only on creation: the schema is all\n    // `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so re-running it against an existing\n    // graph is a no-op for tables that are already there and the\n    // migration path for ones added since that graph was created (the\n    // `debt` table, for instance). `created` still reports whether the\n    // file itself is new.\n    applySchema(db);\n  } finally {\n    db.close();\n  }\n\n  return { created: !already, path: dbPath };\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "src/db/plan.mjs",
      "content": "// `hedgehog plan` — compiles pending intents against the project's core\n// definition into `tasks` + `dependencies` rows. See\n// hedgehog-persistent-build-graph.md, \"The build graph\" and \"Task\n// lifecycle\", plus the readiness SELECT under \"Schema\".\n//\n// full-stack-app and pwa-app: one task per layer per intent (an intent is\n// a domain module — see the core definition's `{module}` placeholder).\n// landing-page, copywriting, deepseek-harness, and authored (whether\n// designed from scratch or adopted onto an existing repo): one task per\n// phase/layer, no module axis. All are the same operation — walk a core\n// definition's layer chain once per intent — because a linear chain is\n// the degenerate case of the layer graph (spec: MVP scope item 5).\n//\n// Layer cardinality: a layer marked `once: true` in the core definition\n// opts out of that per-intent multiplication and compiles a single task\n// for the whole build. It's how a module-axis core expresses genuinely\n// cross-cutting work — provisioning a cluster, deploying the built\n// system — that is one piece of work no matter how many modules the\n// graph holds. Without it such a layer compiles once per intent and\n// every copy but the first is a replay of the same command.\n\nimport { composeScope } from './overrides.mjs';\n\nexport function fillModule(template, module) {\n  return template.replaceAll('{module}', module);\n}\n\n// Deterministic, human-legible task id: <INTENT>-<LAYER>, upper-cased.\n// Stable across repeated `hedgehog plan` runs on the same intent/layer.\nexport function taskId(intentId, layerId) {\n  return `${intentId}-${layerId}`.toUpperCase();\n}\n\n// A `once: true` layer's task id is the bare layer id — no intent\n// prefix, because there is no intent it belongs to. The missing prefix\n// is the signal: `DEPLOY` is the build's one deploy, `ORDERS-DEPLOY`\n// would be one of several.\nexport function onceTaskId(layerId) {\n  return layerId.toUpperCase();\n}\n\n// The once-layer counterpart to layerTaskFields: what a once: true\n// layer contributes to its single task row. No {module} substitution —\n// a once-layer has no module to substitute (core.mjs's validateCore\n// rejects one that names {module}) — so this can't share\n// layerTaskFields's body, only its role as the one place drift.mjs and\n// the compiler both read from.\n//\n// `overrides` (a Map from overrides.mjs#loadOverrides, keyed by task id —\n// here always onceTaskId(layer.id)) is composed in last, via\n// composeScope, so a hand-authored .hedgehog/overrides/*.json entry\n// widens scope_globs the same way for a once-task as for a per-intent\n// one. Defaults to an empty Map so every existing caller that doesn't\n// pass one keeps computing the un-widened fields.\nexport function onceLayerTaskFields(layer, overrides = new Map()) {\n  const fields = {\n    objective: `${layer.id} for the whole build`,\n    scope_globs: JSON.stringify(layer.scope),\n    verify_command: layer.verify,\n    commit_message: layer.commit,\n    exclusive: layer.exclusive ? 1 : 0,\n    verify_radius: layer.verify_radius === null ? null : JSON.stringify(layer.verify_radius),\n  };\n  return composeScope(fields, onceTaskId(layer.id), overrides);\n}\n\n// `tasks.intent_id` is NOT NULL and a foreign key into `intents`, so a\n// once-layer's task still needs an intent to hang off. Attributing it to\n// a real intent is what this feature exists to stop — it would put\n// cluster provisioning under whichever module happened to compile first,\n// link it to that module's requirements, and hold that intent open until\n// the infrastructure ran. So the compiler synthesises one intent, owned\n// by the core rather than by any module. It is derived entirely from\n// core.yaml, which makes it reproducible by `hedgehog db rebuild`\n// (whereas \"the first intent compiled\" is not: intent order changes as\n// intents are added, so a rebuild could attribute the same task\n// differently). No `.hedgehog/intents/*.json` backs it — core.yaml is\n// its committed source.\nexport const CORE_INTENT_ID = '_core';\n\n// Also `tasks.module` for every once-layer task: the value that would be\n// substituted into {module} if a once-layer were allowed to carry one\n// (core.mjs's validateCore rejects that). next.mjs reads it to know a\n// packet is cross-cutting rather than module-scoped.\nexport const CORE_MODULE = CORE_INTENT_ID;\n\n// Once-layer tasks take the schema's default intent priority. Ordering\n// between a once-layer and the modules around it is carried by the\n// dependency edges, not by priority — a head once-layer is upstream of\n// every module's first layer, and a tail one is downstream of every\n// module's last.\nconst CORE_INTENT_PRIORITY = 100;\n\nfunction coreIntent(core) {\n  return {\n    id: CORE_INTENT_ID,\n    goal: `Cross-cutting layers of core \"${core.id}\"`,\n    outcome: `Each once: true layer of \"${core.id}\" is built exactly once for the whole build, not once per module`,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction layerById(core) {\n  return new Map(core.layers.map((layer) => [layer.id, layer]));\n}\n\n// Compiles the core's `once: true` layers — one task each, for the whole\n// build — plus the edges between two once-layers. Edges that cross the\n// cardinality boundary in either direction are per-intent and belong to\n// compileIntentTasks. Independent of the intent set entirely, which is\n// what makes the result identical on every run.\nfunction compileOnceTasks(core, overrides) {\n  const byId = layerById(core);\n  const onceLayers = core.layers.filter((layer) => layer.once);\n\n  const tasks = onceLayers.map((layer) => ({\n    id: onceTaskId(layer.id),\n    intent_id: CORE_INTENT_ID,\n    module: CORE_MODULE,\n    layer: layer.id,\n    priority: CORE_INTENT_PRIORITY,\n    ...onceLayerTaskFields(layer, overrides),\n  }));\n\n  const dependencies = [];\n  for (const layer of onceLayers) {\n    if (!layer.depends_on) continue;\n    if (!byId.get(layer.depends_on).once) continue; // per-intent parent — see compileIntentTasks\n    dependencies.push({\n      task_id: onceTaskId(layer.id),\n      depends_on_task_id: onceTaskId(layer.depends_on),\n    });\n  }\n\n  return { tasks, dependencies };\n}\n\n// Compiles one intent's tasks + the dependencies that intent contributes,\n// without touching the database. Only the core's per-intent layers become\n// tasks here; `once: true` layers are compiled separately, exactly once,\n// by compileOnceTasks.\n//\n// Three of the four `depends_on` combinations are this function's, one\n// row per intent:\n//   per-intent → per-intent   this intent's chain link (the original case)\n//   per-intent → once         every module's task waits on the single\n//                             once-task, so a head infra layer gates the\n//                             whole build\n//   once → per-intent         the single once-task waits on this intent's\n//                             task — repeated across intents, it becomes\n//                             \"waits on all of them\", so a tail deploy\n//                             layer runs after every module has landed\n// The fourth (once → once) is compileOnceTasks's, since it has no\n// per-intent multiplicity.\n\n// The `tasks` columns whose value is derived purely from the core\n// definition's layer (plus the module it's being instantiated for) —\n// i.e. everything `plan` copies out of core.yaml and that a later\n// core.yaml edit therefore leaves stale.       "content": "// The host registry: one entry per coding agent Hedgehog installs into.\n//\n// A host describes where the discipline's payload lands in a consuming\n// repo and, where the host's format differs from the canonical one, how\n// to emit it. `src/agents/` and `src/skills/` are the single source of\n// truth for content — a host adapts packaging, never substance.\n//\n// Adding a host means adding one entry here (and a matching directory\n// under src/hosts/<name>/ for whatever templates it needs).\n\nimport { emitPromptAgent, emitOpencodeAgent } from './emit.mjs';\n\n// Hosts that dispatch real subagents get the full discipline: each build\n// step runs in its own context with its own role. Hosts that don't are\n// still supported through the AGENTS.md routing doc, which indexes the\n// same agent and skill files for an agent to read inline. Either way\n// `hedgehog verify` is what gates a commit, so correctness does not\n// depend on the host's tool grants.\n\n/**\n * @typedef {object} Host\n * @property {string} agentsDir      where agent definitions land\n * @property {string} skillsDir      where skill directories land\n * @property {string} bootstrapFile  the project file this host auto-loads\n * @property {(body: string, meta: object) => string} [emitAgent]\n *   rewrites one agent file for this host. Omitted when the canonical\n *   file is already in the host's format — the installer then copies it\n *   verbatim, which is what keeps Claude Code output byte-identical.\n * @property {Array<object>} [extraEntries] extra payload entries for this host\n */\n\n// AGENTS.md is the convention a growing number of coding agents read\n// from a repo root. Every host ships it: it costs one generated file and\n// it means a second agent opening the project finds the discipline\n// without a second install.\nconst routingDoc = (host) => ({\n  type: 'generated',\n  to: 'AGENTS.md',\n  // Indexes every host the project is set up for, not just the one being\n  // installed, so adding a second host doesn't strand the first one's\n  // paths.\n  generate: async ({ pkgRoot, projectRoot }) => {\n    const [{ renderAgentsMd }, { installedHosts }] = await Promise.all([\n      import('./routing.mjs'),\n      import('./installed.mjs'),\n    ]);\n    const recorded = projectRoot ? await installedHosts(projectRoot) : [];\n    const names = [...new Set([host, ...recorded])];\n    return renderAgentsMd({ pkgRoot, hosts: names.map((n) => HOSTS[n]) });\n  },\n});\n\n/** @type {Record<string, Host>} */\nexport const HOSTS = {\n  // Claude Code reads src/agents/*.md and src/skills/ * /SKILL.md as\n  // authored — frontmatter and all — so it has no emitter. This is the\n  // canonical format every other host is adapted from.\n  claude: {\n    agentsDir: '.claude/agents',\n    skillsDir: '.claude/skills',\n    bootstrapFile: 'CLAUDE.md',\n    label: 'Claude Code',\n    get extraEntries() {\n      return [routingDoc('claude')];\n    },\n  },\n\n  // Cursor loads `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` on every request and reads\n  // AGENTS.md at the repo root. The rule points at both, the project's\n  // own context lives in HEDGEHOG.md, and the agent files carry their\n  // tool grant as a line of the prompt.\n  cursor: {\n    agentsDir: '.cursor/agents',\n    skillsDir: '.cursor/skills',\n    bootstrapFile: 'HEDGEHOG.md',\n    label: 'Cursor',\n    emitAgent: emitPromptAgent,\n    get extraEntries() {\n      return [\n        routingDoc('cursor'),\n        {\n          type: 'file',\n          from: 'src/hosts/cursor/hedgehog.mdc',\n          to: '.cursor/rules/hedgehog.mdc',\n        },\n      ];\n    },\n  },\n\n  // Gemini CLI loads GEMINI.md at session start and resolves its `@./`\n  // includes, so the routing doc comes in with it. `invoke_agent`\n  // dispatches an untyped generalist, so each agent file carries its\n  // tool grant as a line of the prompt it will be passed as.\n  gemini: {\n    agentsDir: '.gemini/agents',\n    skillsDir: '.gemini/skills',\n    bootstrapFile: 'GEMINI.md',\n    label: 'Gemini CLI',\n    emitAgent: emitPromptAgent,\n    get extraEntries() {\n      return [\n        routingDoc('gemini'),\n        {\n          type: 'file',\n          from: 'src/hosts/gemini/gemini-extension.json',\n          to: 'gemini-extension.json',\n        },\n      ];\n    },\n  },\n\n  // OpenCode auto-loads AGENTS.md from the repo root — the same file\n  // every host ships as an index. The bootstrap merge carries the\n  // discipline shell and the dispatch into it directly, so no separate\n  // routing doc is generated and the file has one writer per install\n  // flag. Subagents register from `.opencode/agents/` (the file name is\n  // the agent name; Claude Code's `model:`/`tools:` subagent schema\n  // comes off on install), and skills load on demand from\n  // `.opencode/skills/`.\n  opencode: {\n    agentsDir: '.opencode/agents',\n    skillsDir: '.opencode/skills',\n    bootstrapFile: 'AGENTS.md',\n    label: 'OpenCode',\n    emitAgent: emitOpencodeAgent,\n  },\n\n  // Windsurf (Devin Desktop) auto-loads AGENTS.md from the repo root as\n  // an always-on instruction file. The bootstrap merge carries the\n  // discipline shell and dispatch into it directly. Subagents register\n  // from `.devin/agents/` with their tool grant in the prompt, and\n  // skills load from `.devin/skills/`.\n  windsurf: {\n    agentsDir: '.devin/agents',\n    skillsDir: '.devin/skills',\n    bootstrapFile: 'AGENTS.md',\n    label: 'Windsurf',\n    emitAgent: emitPromptAgent,\n  },\n\n  // GitHub Copilot loads `.github/copilot-instructions.md` as its\n  // repo-wide instructions, so the discipline shell and dispatch land\n  // there, and the generated AGENTS.md indexes the roles. Custom agents\n  // register from `.github/agents/` (the file name is the agent name)\n  // with their tool grant in the prompt, and skills load from\n  // `.github/skills/`.\n  copilot: {\n    agentsDir: '.github/agents',\n    skillsDir: '.github/skills',\n    bootstrapFile: '.github/copilot-instructions.md',\n    label: 'GitHub Copilot',\n    emitAgent: emitPromptAgent,\n    get extraEntries() {\n      return [routingDoc('copilot')];\n    },\n  },\n};\n\n// One install flag per host, named for the tool a user is asking to use.\n// Mirrors CORE_FLAGS in bin/cli.mjs: the public flag and the internal\n// name are allowed to diverge so the CLI surface can stay stable.\nexport const HOST_FLAGS = {\n  '--claude': 'claude',\n  '--cursor': 'cursor',\n  '--gemini': 'gemini',\n  '--opencode': 'opencode',\n  '--windsurf': 'windsurf',\n  '--copilot': 'copilot',\n};\n\nexport const DEFAULT_HOST = 'claude';\n\nexport const availableHosts = () => Object.keys(HOSTS).sort();\n"
    },
