      "path": "src/registry/cores.json",
      "content": "{\n  \"cores\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"full-stack-app\",\n      \"flag\": \"--ts-full-stack-app\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-full-stack-app\",\n      \"version\": \"^1.1.0\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-full-stack-app\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"The description names server-side logic across most of the app: authorization more expressive than per-object row-level security, background jobs, scheduled work or webhook receivers as the app's primary function, server-rendered or SEO-critical pages beyond an app shell, or a data model whose working set doesn't sensibly fit on a device. Persistent domain data alone is not the signal — a tracker, journal, notebook, or planner whose data fits on the user's device is pwa-app, even with sharing, accounts, or multi-device sync in scope, and even with one or two entities that must be server-authoritative. If the project has both a marketing page and a real app behind it, this is still full-stack-app: the page becomes routes inside apps/web, not a separate project.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"pwa-app\",\n      \"flag\": \"--pwa-app\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-pwa-app\",\n      \"version\": \"^1.1.0\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-pwa-app\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"The description names an app whose data model fits on the user's device and whose reads and writes are the user's own — a tracker, journal, notebook, planner, offline reference, or utility. Offline capability or installability named explicitly is a strong signal. Sharing, collaboration, accounts, and multi-device sync do NOT disqualify a project: Dexie Cloud provides sync, authentication, and server-enforced per-object access control, so a shared list, a family calendar, or a small team's board is still this core. A small number of entities that must be server-authoritative — a points balance, a reward ledger, anything a client must not write to directly — do NOT disqualify a project either: those entities are declared --remote and backed by Supabase (Postgres + RLS + Edge Functions) behind the same repository interface, while the rest of the app stays local-first. What routes a project to full-stack-app is server-side logic across most of the app, not the presence of one or two such entities: authorization beyond row-level policies, background jobs or webhooks as the app's primary function, server-rendered pages, or a working set too large for a device.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"landing-page\",\n      \"flag\": \"--landing-page\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-landing-page\",\n      \"version\": \"^1.0.2\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-landing-page\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"The description is a marketing/announcement/waitlist/portfolio page (or a small handful of such pages) with no persistent domain data of its own. A page that only collects an email into a third-party form service, or has no state at all, qualifies. The bar is \\\"no domain module\\\" — a landing page with a dozen sections is still landing-page, not promoted to full-stack-app for being long.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"deepseek-harness\",\n      \"flag\": \"--deepseek-harness\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-deepseek-harness\",\n      \"version\": \">=0.2.3 <1.0.0\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-deepseek-harness\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"The description names building a plugin, tool, hook, or extension for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) — a Cordis-based agent framework — or otherwise extending an existing DSH installation with new capabilities via its plugin/bundle system. Concrete signals: DSH, DeepSeek Harness, Cordis, `defineTool`, `ctx.tools.register`, a `cordis.patch.yml` manifest, or a request to add a tool that a DSH agent can call. This is the core most often confused with authored: authored fits when no shipped core matches and the planner must design a system shape from scratch, but a DSH plugin already has a fixed, battle-tested shape (the six-layer scaffold → logic → wiring → smoke → bundle → join sequence, one plugin per intent) that authored's from-scratch design would only reinvent worse. Route here whenever the target of the work is a DSH plugin, not a general \\\"no other core fits\\\" fallback.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"authored\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-authored\",\n      \"version\": \"^1.2.0\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-authored\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"Neither shipped core fits, but the description names a real artifact a Builder step would produce — just not in either shipped core's shape. This core is designed by the planner rather than chosen from a fixed set: hedgehog-planning-intake's Phase 0 elicits the drivers first, then hedgehog-core-design names the system shape, picks the stack, derives the layers, and writes .hedgehog/core.yaml. It carries the same enforcement as a shipped core — ordered layers, scoped file access, verification before completion — but the sequence is designed for this project rather than battle-tested across many. This is the core most often confused with adopted: authored designs a workspace from scratch for a project being built new, while adopted brings Hedgehog's discipline to a repo that already exists — route here only when there is no existing codebase this work is being added to.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"adopted\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-adopted\",\n      \"version\": \">=1.0.0 <2.0.0\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-adopted\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"The description is about bringing Hedgehog's discipline to a codebase that already exists, rather than building something new — the repo already has real source files, or the user says so explicitly: \\\"adopt this repo\\\", \\\"add Hedgehog to my existing project\\\", \\\"I want scope/verify enforcement on my changes here\\\". Not chosen by matching a `when` paragraph the way a shipped core is: hedgehog-adopt reads the repo read-only, proposes a linear-chain .hedgehog/core.yaml whose verify commands are the repo's own, and writes only .hedgehog/ — never a workspace, never a stack migration. This is the core most often confused with authored: adopted brings discipline to an existing repo, while authored designs and scaffolds a workspace from scratch for something being built new — route here only when the work is landing on a codebase that already exists.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"copywriting\",\n      \"flag\": \"--copywriting\",\n      \"package\": \"@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-copywriting-prose-engineering\",\n      \"version\": \"^0.2.0\",\n      \"language\": \"typescript\",\n      \"repository\": \"https://github.com/skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-copywriting-prose-engineering\",\n      \"selects_when\": \"The description asks for a piece of writing or prose to be written or fixed as its own deliverable — marketing copy, a product announcement, UI microcopy strings, docs prose, an email, a pitch, an article, an essay, a blog post, or any other standalone written piece — with no page, app, or other artifact being built around it. Concrete signals: \\\"write an article about X\\\", \\\"write copy for X\\\", \\\"help me write a blog post\\\", \\\"make this sound less like AI\\\", \\\"fix this copy\\\", \\\"improve this writing\\\", \\\"draft a product announcement\\\", a request to run text through an AI-tell or humanizer check. Not just marketing/product framing — any standalone prose request qualifies, articles and essays included. The core drafts against `checkCopy()`, a real script running deterministic AI-tell and prose-quality checks (banned vocabulary, passive voice, readability score, sentence-length variance), not an agent's own self-review — a piece of writing ships because the script exited 0. This is the core most often confused with landing-page: landing-page's own copy skill still owns copy that's part of a full page build (headline, hero, section copy sequenced through that core's Chain Method); route here only when the writing is the entire ask, not one stage of a larger build.\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n"

      "path": "src/registry/fetch.mjs",
      "content": "// Fetches a core package and reads its manifest.\n//\n// A core ships as its own npm package (see cores.json) carrying the\n// agents, skills, workspace, and CLAUDE.md section that core needs.\n// `fetchCore` resolves that package with `npm pack`, extracts the tarball,\n// and returns the parsed `hedgehog-core.yaml` manifest alongside the\n// directory it was extracted to — everything `init` needs to plan its\n// writes against a core it did not ship with.\n//\n// Extractions are cached at ~/.hedgehog/cores/<name>/<version>/, keyed by\n// the exact version npm resolved rather than the range asked for, so a\n// second install of the same core is a directory read with no network.\n\nimport { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, readdir, rm, rename, access } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { constants } from 'node:fs';\nimport { execFile } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { promisify } from 'node:util';\nimport { tmpdir, homedir } from 'node:os';\nimport { join } from 'node:path';\nimport { parseCoreManifest, assertEngineSatisfies } from './manifest.mjs';\n\nconst execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);\n\n// The CLI's own version, which a core's `engine` range is checked against\n// every time a manifest is read.\nconst ENGINE_VERSION = JSON.parse(\n  await readFile(new URL('../../package.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8'),\n).version;\n\nconst MANIFEST_NAME = 'hedgehog-core.yaml';\n\n// npm's own tarball root — every published package extracts under this.\nconst TARBALL_ROOT = 'package';\n\nexport const CORE_CACHE_ROOT = join(homedir(), '.hedgehog', 'cores');\n\n// Resolution source for core packages. Unset, cores resolve from the\n// public npm registry by their `package` and `version` in cores.json. Set\n// to a directory, each core resolves from `<dir>/<package-basename>`\n// instead — a local checkout or a packed tarball — which is how a core is\n// exercised end to end before it is published.\nconst SOURCE_ENV = 'HEDGEHOG_CORE_SOURCE';\n\n// Skip cache (both reads and writes) when set; every invocation gets a fresh\n// npm pack with no persistence to ~/.hedgehog/cores/. Useful when the\n// caller's use of the fetched core is ephemeral or when accurate npm\n// download stats are needed.\nconst NO_CACHE_ENV = 'HEDGEHOG_CORE_NO_CACHE';\n\nconst exists = (p) =>\n  access(p, constants.F_OK).then(\n    () => true,\n    () => false,\n  );\n\n// What `npm pack` is asked to resolve for this core: a registry spec, or\n// a local path under HEDGEHOG_CORE_SOURCE named for the package's last\n// path segment (`@skyf0xx/hedgehog-core-landing-page` →\n// `hedgehog-core-landing-page`).\nfunction packSpec(entry) {\n  const source = process.env[SOURCE_ENV];\n  if (!source) return `${entry.package}@${entry.version}`;\n  return join(source, entry.package.split('/').pop());\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve, extract, and read one core package.\n *\n * @param {object} entry - a cores.json entry (`name`, `package`, `version`)\n * @returns {Promise<{manifest: object, root: string, version: string,\n *   engineAdvisory: string|null}>} the parsed hedgehog-core.yaml, the\n *   directory the package extracted to, the exact version resolved, and a\n *   line to print when the CLI is ahead of the core's engine line.\n */\nexport async function fetchCore(entry) {\n  const staged = await packAndExtract(entry);\n  const version = await packageVersion(staged.root);\n  const cached = join(CORE_CACHE_ROOT, entry.name, version);\n\n  // Read the manifest off the staged copy first. The cache is what\n  // `cores list` reports as reusable and what an offline `update` reads\n  // back, so only a core this engine can actually install belongs in it —\n  // a manifest that fails here throws before anything is cached.\n  let read;\n  try {\n    read = await readManifest(staged.root, entry);\n  } catch (err) {\n    await rm(staged.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    throw err;\n  }\n\n  // When NO_CACHE_ENV is set, skip cache entirely and return the staged\n  // extraction directly, leaving staged.tmp in place (since staged.root\n  // lives inside it).\n  if (process.env[NO_CACHE_ENV]) {\n    return { ...read, root: staged.root, version };\n  }\n\n  // Another install may have cached this exact version between the pack\n  // and now; its copy is as good as this one, so keep it and drop ours.\n  if (await exists(cached)) {\n    await rm(staged.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    return { ...read, root: cached, version };\n  }\n\n  await mkdir(join(CORE_CACHE_ROOT, entry.name), { recursive: true });\n  await rename(staged.root, cached);\n  await rm(staged.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });\n  return { ...read, root: cached, version };\n}\n\n/**\n * The cached extraction for a core at a given version, or null when that\n * version has never been fetched. Lets a caller that already knows which\n * version it wants — `update`, reading the version a project recorded —\n * work offline without asking npm to resolve anything.\n */\nexport async function cachedCore(entry, version) {\n  const root = join(CORE_CACHE_ROOT, entry.name, version);\n  if (!(await exists(join(root, MANIFEST_NAME)))) return null;\n  return { ...(await readManifest(root, entry)), root, version };\n}\n\nasync function packAndExtract(entry) {\n  const spec = packSpec(entry);\n  const tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), `hedgehog-core-${entry.name}-`));\n\n  let tarball;\n  try {\n    const { stdout } = await execFileAsync(\n      'npm',\n      ['pack', spec, '--pack-destination', tmp, '--json', '--loglevel', 'error'],\n      { cwd: tmp, maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 },\n    );\n    tarball = join(tmp, JSON.parse(stdout)[0].filename);\n  } catch (err) {\n    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    throw new Error(unresolvableMessage(entry, spec, err), { cause: err });\n  }\n\n  try {\n    await execFileAsync('tar', ['-xzf', tarball, '-C', tmp]);\n  } catch (err) {\n    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    throw new Error(`Could not extract ${entry.package} from ${tarball}: ${err.message}`, { cause: err });\n  }\n\n  const root = join(tmp, TARBALL_ROOT);\n  if (!(await exists(join(root, MANIFEST_NAME)))) {\n    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    throw new Error(\n      `${entry.package} carries no ${MANIFEST_NAME}, so there is nothing to install from it.\\n` +\n        `Every Hedgehog core package ships that manifest at its root; a package without one\\n` +\n        `is not a core. Check the package name in the registry entry for \"${entry.name}\".`,\n    );\n  }\n  return { tmp, root };\n}\n\nasync function packageVersion(root) {\n  const { version } = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));\n  return version;\n}\n\nasync function readManifest(root, entry) {\n  const manifest = parseCoreManifest(\n    await readFile(join(root, MANIFEST_NAME), 'utf8'),\n    `${entry.package}/${MANIFEST_NAME}`,\n  );\n  if (manifest.name !== entry.name) {\n    throw new Error(\n      `${entry.package} declares core \"${manifest.name}\", but the registry lists it as \"${entry.name}\".\\n` +\n        `The package and the registry entry have to agree on the core's name.`,\n    );\n  }\n  const engineAdvisory = assertEngineSatisfies(\n    manifest,\n    ENGINE_VERSION,\n    `${entry.package}/${MANIFEST_NAME}`,\n  );\n  return { manifest, engineAdvisory };\n}\n\n// npm's own failure text is a wall of registry detail; what a user can act\n// on is which package could not be resolved and the two reasons it usually\n// can't be.\nfunction unresolvableMessage(entry, spec, err) {\n  const detail = String(err.stderr || err.message).trim().split('\\n').slice(0, 3).join('\\n  ');\n  return (\n    `Could not resolve the ${entry.name} core package (${spec}).\\n\\n` +\n    `  ${detail}\\n\\n` +\n    `That package carries the core's workspace, agents, and skills. Check that you\\n` +\n    `are online and that npm can reach the registry, then re-run. To resolve from a\\n` +\n    `local checkout or a packed tarball instead, point ${SOURCE_ENV} at the\\n` +\n    `directory holding it.`\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * The engine line the newest cached extraction of a core declares, or\n * null when that core has never been fetched. `cores list` reports it so\n * the engine line each core is written against is visible at the point a\n * core is chosen, rather than only once an install has run.\n */\nexport async function cachedEngine(name, versions) {\n  const newest = [...versions].sort(compareVersions).pop();\n  if (!newest) return null;\n  try {\n    const text = await readFile(join(CORE_CACHE_ROOT, name, newest, MANIFEST_NAME), 'utf8');\n    return parseCoreManifest(text, `${name}/${MANIFEST_NAME}`).engine ?? null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n// Orders `1.0.5` after `1.0.0` rather than before it, which a plain\n// string sort would not.\nfunction compareVersions(a, b) {\n  const parts = (v) => String(v).split('.').map(Number);\n  const [x, y] = [parts(a), parts(b)];\n  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {\n    if ((x[i] ?? 0) !== (y[i] ?? 0)) return (x[i] ?? 0) - (y[i] ?? 0);\n  }\n  return 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * List which versions of a core are already extracted in the cache.\n * Reported by `hedgehog cores list` so a user can see what an install\n * would reuse rather than fetch.\n */\nexport async function cachedVersions(name) {\n  try {\n    return (await readdir(join(CORE_CACHE_ROOT, name), { withFileTypes: true }))\n      .filter((e) => e.isDirectory())\n      .map((e) => e.name)\n      .sort();\n  } catch {\n    return [];\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "src/skills/hedgehog-orchestrating/SKILL.md",
      "content": "---\nname: hedgehog-orchestrating\ndescription: Use at the start of any session on a project with a build graph (`.hedgehog/hedgehog.db`), and again at every claim/dispatch/verify cycle within it. Owns consuming the build graph — claiming task packets, delegating each to the layer's agent, running `hedgehog verify` to gate the commit, recording debt and decisions, the intent check at an intent's last layer, and when to clear context. Not for a build agent handed an already-claimed packet — that agent never claims, dispatches, or verifies; this skill is the orchestrating session's own.\n---\n\n# Orchestrating the build\n\n`.hedgehog/hedgehog.db` is the source of truth for what's next — never\nre-derive build state from prose. To work from it:\n\n1. Run `hedgehog claim --count N --owner <owner>`. It's atomic and\n   lease-based, and returns up to N tasks (each with its own full\n   STATUS/INTENT/RELEVANT RULES/INHERITED DEBT/INHERITED DECISIONS/WHY\n   NOW/BLOCKED DOWNSTREAM/ALLOWED SCOPE/VERIFICATION packet) that the\n   scheduler has already verified are safe to run together right now —\n   scope and verify-radius disjoint. `--count` is a maximum, not a\n   promise: a call may return fewer than N, or zero. `hedgehog ready` is\n   a read-only preview of the claimable/held-back split (and why a task\n   is held back — conflict with another claimable task, or exclusivity)\n   before you claim.\n2. Delegate each claimed packet to this core's loop skill (named in the\n   project's core section), one dispatch per packet, running concurrently.\n3. As each agent reports its packet done, run `hedgehog verify\n   <task-id> --owner <owner>` **serially** — one at a time, even though\n   the building happened concurrently, because verify writes git commits\n   and those must land one at a time. It checks the touched files\n   against the packet's ALLOWED SCOPE, runs the verification command,\n   and on a pass writes the commit and unlocks whatever the task was\n   blocking. An agent reporting success never moves the task — only a\n   passing `hedgehog verify` exit code does.\n\n`hedgehog claim` hands out only tasks safe to run together. Never run\ntwo tasks it didn't hand you together.\n\nThe packet's **INTENT** block names the goal and outcome of the *whole*\nintent, not just this layer. A layer's own verify command runs the tests\nthat layer wrote, so it measures internal consistency and never coverage\nof what was asked — a layer that builds half the intent and tests that\nhalf exhaustively is green.
